newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Three Gorges developer eyes overseas bonds.
newsitem.headline: China Three Gorges developer eyes overseas bonds.

text.p: The company developing China's Three Gorges dam does not rule out issuing bonds overseas to supplement development capital needed to build the world's largest hydroelectric dam, senior executives said on Thursday.

"This (overseas bonds issues) must be approved by the central government, but in my personal opinion we must use foreign funds," Qin Zhongyi, vice president of China Yangtze Three Gorges Project Development Corp, said in Hong Kong.

"That's because the interest on domestic bonds is high," Qin told a news conference. "In the domestic market, projects are in search of capital, but overseas, capital is looking for projects to invest in."
Interest or coupon rates on overseas issues were much lower, Qin added.
"Add to that the fact that the Three Gorges project is a good investment opportunity, and overseas firms are willing to invest in it," he said.
Qin said the project received export credits for machinery and equipment purchases and would publicly list certain operations, in addition to pursuing other financing methods.
The company had previously discussed bond issues with U.S. investment banks Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch, Qin said, but did not give any further details.
Qin said the project was not cash needy at present.

Its major funding came chiefly from three sources, the Three Gorges Project Construction Fund, one billion yuan in annual revenue from the Gezhouba Power Plant, and a State Development Bank loan which provided three billion yuan a year, Qin said.
This provided a total of eight billion yuan a year, he added.
The project also received the proceeds from one billion yuan three-year domestic bonds, issued in March 1996
Gezhouba Co Ltd, which started trading on the Shanghai exchange on Thursday, is not a part of the group.
